findings.claim: The row's back-seam warrant names a fear-not formula as the onset signal at web:Isa.44.1, but no fear-not formula stands in that verse's bytes in either witness.
findings.grounds: The shipped prose reads 'just ahead of the fresh fear-not address to “Jacob my servant” that opens web:Isa.44.1'. MT 44:1 in full is וְעַתָּ֥ה שְׁמַ֖ע יַעֲקֹ֣ב עַבְדִּ֑י וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּחַ֥רְתִּי בֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.44.1, byte tier), whose onset run is וְעַתָּ֥ה שְׁמַ֖ע (oshb:Isa.44.1, byte tier) — an adversative plus imperative — and WEB 44:1 reads “Yet listen now, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen.” (web:Isa.44.1). The fear-not formula stands one verse later: אַל תִּירָא֙ (oshb:Isa.44.2, byte tier), a pair re-collated here as byte-identical to the fear-not opening the address at oshb:Isa.43.1 (byte tier). The book-order neighbour row argues this same seam incompatibly, stating that the divine frame and the fear-not it governs stand one verse inside its unit rather than at its onset, so the two rows locate one formula at two different verses. The named-servant half of the descriptor is byte-true at 44:1, and the seam itself survives on the adversative-plus-imperative onset, on the closing verdict at web:Isa.43.28 and on the disclosed SAMEKH at MT 43:28, so the defect lies in the stated warrant rather than in the cut.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale: replace 'the fresh fear-not address ... that opens web:Isa.44.1' with the onset signal actually standing in that verse — the adversative-plus-imperative וְעַתָּ֥ה שְׁמַ֖ע (oshb:Isa.44.1, byte tier) with its named-servant address — and, if the fear-not is cited at all, locate it at oshb:Isa.44.2 with web:Isa.44.2 added to boundary_evidence_refs.

findings.claim: A byte-true catchword straddles the row's own front seam and is disclosed nowhere in the row.
findings.grounds: The declaring root stands at exactly two verses across chapters 43-44 (sweep: 2 verses; count object: skeleton, word-unbound contiguous consonantal substring): יְסַפֵּֽרוּ (oshb:Isa.43.21, byte tier), the last word of the verse immediately outside the row's front seam, and סַפֵּ֥ר (oshb:Isa.43.26, byte tier), inside the row's own span. The row cites oshb:Isa.43.21 in its own prose for a different purpose and never discloses the device crossing its front seam, while sibling rows in the same book-order run disclose the analogous forming-root and redeemer catchwords explicitly.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to device_notes: disclose the declaring-root catchword across the front seam with both splices, its digit and count object named, and the tier stated as root/skeleton level rather than a repeated form.

findings.claim: The row's cross-seam catchword disclosure labels the two witness forms as matching at skeleton tier only, but they are not identical at skeleton tier.
findings.grounds: The two spliced runs are וְאַתֶּ֣ם עֵדָ֑י (oshb:Isa.44.8, byte tier) and וְעֵדֵיהֶ֣ם הֵׄ֗מָּׄהׄ (oshb:Isa.44.9, byte tier). Their skeletons, taken from the staged consonantal layer, are distinct strings, and so are the skeletons of the two witness tokens alone — עֵדָ֑י (oshb:Isa.44.8, byte tier) against וְעֵדֵיהֶ֣ם (oshb:Isa.44.9, byte tier). The relation is root sharing with containment of the shorter skeleton inside the longer, not skeleton-tier identity; the row's own added clause about sharing the same witness root states the true relation, and the tier label then overstates it. The book-order neighbour rows state the structurally identical redeemer catchword correctly, as sharing a root in different conjugations and not identical at byte, accent-stripped or skeleton tier.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to device_notes: strike 'and matching at skeleton tier only', state the relation as root-level with containment of the shorter skeleton, and add skeleton to the existing non-identity list alongside byte, nfd and accent-stripped.

findings.claim: The row disambiguates the rock epithet against the adversary and Tyre homographs 'sharing its skeleton', but neither shares that skeleton, and the claim ships without a digit or a named count object.
findings.grounds: The row's own splice is צ֖וּר (oshb:Isa.44.8, byte tier). Tyre stands as צֹ֑ר (oshb:Isa.23.1, byte tier) at the head of its own oracle, and its two-consonant skeleton is not a contiguous substring of the rock epithet's three-consonant skeleton; the adversary and narrow family carries that same two-consonant skeleton. A word-unbound contiguous skeleton sweep on the rock epithet's consonants returns 23 verses (sweep: 23 verses; count object: skeleton substring), and the chapter-23 Tyre oracle verses are absent from that list. The verses that genuinely share the skeleton are the besieged, fortified, reaping and refining families — for example נְצוּרָֽה (oshb:Isa.1.8, byte tier) and מָצ֑וֹר (oshb:Isa.19.6, byte tier) — alongside the rock-epithet sites themselves. The disambiguation therefore names two classes that are not skeleton-sharers and omits the class that is.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale: either drop the homograph clause, or restate it against the classes that actually share the epithet's skeleton with a digit and count object named, keeping the Tyre and adversary contrast only if labelled a pointed-form contrast rather than a skeleton one.

findings.claim: A curly-quoted WEB English run and an English content reference are both cited to the Hebrew witness.
findings.grounds: The shipped prose reads 'The blotted-transgression announcement closes at “Return to me, for I have redeemed you.” (oshb:Isa.44.22), and the row's own final verse sits just before the heavens' song that opens oshb:Isa.44.23'. The quoted English is WEB wording and is verbatim at web:Isa.44.22; the Hebrew actually standing at that ref is שׁוּבָ֥ה אֵלַ֖י כִּ֥י גְאַלְתִּֽיךָ (oshb:Isa.44.22, byte tier). The parashah citation later in the same sentence is correctly MT-keyed, so the oshb: prefix is right for the mark and wrong for the English quote and the English heavens'-song reference. The field does carry web: refs elsewhere, so the defect is the quote-adjacent attribution rather than a missing witness.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale: re-tag the English quote as (web:Isa.44.22) and the heavens'-song reference as web:Isa.44.23, leaving the petuchah citation at oshb:Isa.44.23 unchanged.

findings.claim: The row states the location and direction of its tier-3 parashah evidence backwards: the petuchah falls on the row's own closing seam and separates the section from the following oracle, rather than sitting on the far side of that seam and grouping the section with it.
findings.grounds: The mark inventory (WLC single witness, MT keys) carries SAMEKH at MT 44:20 and PE at MT 44:23, so the section those marks bound is MT 44:21-44:23 and the PE closes it after 44:23. The row's span is the single verse Isa.44.23-Isa.44.23, whose closing seam is 44:23|44:24 — exactly where that PE falls, not on its far side; and a section end after 44:23 divides 44:21-44:23 from the koh-amar oracle spliced at כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ גֹּאֲלֶ֔ךָ וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ מִבָּ֑טֶן (oshb:Isa.44.24, byte tier) rather than grouping them with it. The layer's real direction is weak corroboration of the row's closing seam together with pressure against its front seam at 44:22|44:23, which is the row's own disclosed rival; the shipped sentence reverses both. The immediately preceding book-order row describes the same section correctly, as running Isa.44.21-Isa.44.23 and grouping its span with the following doxology, so the two rows give incompatible accounts of one mark. The cut is unaffected: the row rests it on the addressee turn at רָנּ֨וּ שָׁמַ֜יִם כִּֽי עָשָׂ֣ה (oshb:Isa.44.23, byte tier) and expressly not on the tier-3 layer.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale: restate the mark as a petuchah closing the MT 44:21-44:23 section at the row's own closing seam, weak tier-3 corroboration of that seam, while grouping the row's verse with the exhortation before it and so running against the row's front seam; retain the existing disclaimer that the cut rests on the addressee turn.

findings.claim: The row makes an exclusivity claim about its ketiv/qere sites without the digit-bearing sweep count the campaign requires.
findings.grounds: The shipped prose reads 'this is the row's only ketiv/qere site, K/Q' at oshb:Isa.44.24, whose K/Q token pair is אתי מֵאִתִּֽי (oshb:Isa.44.24, byte tier). Checked against the K/Q inventory (WLC single witness, MT keys) the claim is true — no K/Q note stands at MT 44:25, 44:26, 44:27 or 44:28 — so this is a disclosure shortfall rather than a false claim. The universals arm flags the bare exclusivity word with no adjacent digit; the row states neither the verse count it swept nor the count object.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale: carry the sanctioned sweep shorthand with the count object named, so the exclusivity claim ships with its digit (K/Q note verses across the row's span) instead of a bare exclusivity word.

findings.claim: An MT-only ketiv/qere apparatus is attributed to the WEB witness in both prose and boundary_evidence_refs.
findings.grounds: The shipped prose reads 'One of the row's verses, web:Isa.45.2, is a ketiv/qere site (K/Q)' and the refs list carries 'web:Isa.45.2 (K/Q)'. The K/Q apparatus is WLC single-witness and MT-keyed, and the WEB substrate carries no such apparatus. The K/Q token pair standing at that verse is אושר אֲיַשֵּׁ֑ר (oshb:Isa.45.2, byte tier). The content of the claim is true and MT 45:2 is the only K/Q verse across Isa 45:1-45:8, and numbering is identity here so the arithmetic is unaffected; the defect is the witness prefix. Sibling rows in the same book-order run cite the same apparatus correctly as oshb:Isa.44.24 (K/Q) and oshb:Isa.44.17 (K/Q), so this row is the outlier.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: re-tag the prose reference and the boundary_evidence_refs entry as oshb:Isa.45.2 (K/Q) to match the sibling rows, and add the single-witness disclosure the apparatus layer requires.

findings.claim: The row holds two independently-marked woe onsets as one unit at confidence high while a span-internal section mark stands at exactly the disclosed rival's split point, and the prose nowhere discloses that the tier-3 layer runs against the merge.
findings.grounds: The row's own two splices are ה֗וֹי רָ֚ב אֶת יֹ֣צְר֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.45.9, byte tier) and ה֛וֹי אֹמֵ֥ר לְאָ֖ב (oshb:Isa.45.10, byte tier), and the book's device spine lists MT 45:9 and MT 45:10 as two separate verse-initial woe-oracle onsets rather than one, so the rival the row discloses rests on a tier-1 signal at 45:10 and not merely on repetition. The mark inventory (WLC single witness, MT keys) additionally carries SAMEKH at MT 45:9: a section end falling inside the row's own span, at precisely the 45:9|45:10 split the rival proposes, with further SAMEKH at MT 45:8 and MT 45:10 leaving each woe standing as its own section in that layer. The row lists all three marks in boundary_evidence_refs but its prose engages none of them and it asserts confidence high. The immediately preceding book-order row meets the structurally identical situation, a SAMEKH at MT 45:7 backing its own isolate-the-closing-verse rival, by holding confidence at medium with the frontier flag set, so the calibration is inconsistent within the run. Tier-3 is never a boundary driver here and the merge remains a legitimate disclosed reading, so this is a calibration and disclosure defect, not a demonstrated boundary error.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: disclose in device_notes that the parashah layer divides the pair at the row's internal 45:9|45:10 point and so argues for the disclosed rival, and step confidence from high to medium with frontier_flag_considered set true, matching the neighbour row's handling of the same situation. No respan proposed.
